text:
Maria Lopez: Heads-up — seeing cross-namespace reads from project:alpha into project:beta since the RBAC refactor yesterday. Not many requests but definitely unexpected.
Ajay Rao: ack. Any audit logs showing who/what bound the keys?
Maria Lopez: found these lines in the audit. looks like the KMS binding job ran and bound a key to the wrong org id.
```
[2026-03-15T12:03:22Z] svc=kms-sync user=system action=bind key=org-beta/kms-key target=workspace:project-alpha principal=svc:runtime-123 outcome=success
[2026-03-15T12:03:22Z] svc=rbac user=system action=grant role=reader scope=workspace:project-alpha principal=svc:runtime-123 outcome=created
```
Taylor Ng: hmm svc:runtime-123 should be scoped to org-beta, not allowed to be bound to project-alpha. Could be a namespace ID collision.
Olivia Chen: @Ajay @Kevin any recent changes in the namespace ID allocator or the KMS syncer?
Kevin Patel: I deployed a small change in the allocator last week to dedupe legacy ids; it touched the ID normalization. Might be related.
Ajay Rao: kms-sync-bot, can you show the last run config and source cluster for the run at 12:03?
kms-sync-bot: last_run_id=run-20260315-1203, source_cluster=us-west-2-sync, config_hash=sha256:ab3f..f2c, mode=incremental
Priya Singh: What’s the blast radius? Which customers/projects might have seen data access?
Maria Lopez: so far only internal test workloads in project-alpha touched an org-beta key. No personal data seen in logs. But binding allowed read role creation.
Taylor Ng: mitigation steps we should take now: 1) revoke the accidental binding 2) revoke tokens for svc:runtime-123 3) roll back allocator change 4) add audit alert for cross-org bindings
Olivia Chen: +1. I can push a quick policy rollback for the allocator now.
Kevin Patel: rolling back allocator normalization to previous tag v2.3.1 — will coordinate with ops.
ops-sre: starting rollback window, will throttle sync jobs and pause kms-sync-runner in us-west-2-sync. ETA 8 mins.
Ajay Rao: Maria — can you open a KMS staging revoke? I’ll request immediate key unbind from the key admin API.
Maria Lopez: done. 
```
POST /kms/admin/unbind
{ "key": "org-beta/kms-key", "target": "workspace:project-alpha", "force": true }
```
Maria Lopez: API call returned 200, unbind accepted. Added a note to the key ACL.
Priya Singh: I’ll create an immediate audit alert rule: "cross_org_kms_bind" => page on first occurrence and create ticket.
Taylor Ng: Also recommend a deny-by-default extra check: when a binding request comes from a syncer, verify the principal's org_id matches the target org_id before creating roles.
Kevin Patel: yep we should add that to the syncer and to the RBAC write path.
Ajay Rao: Forensics: collect the full run logs and list of principals bound in the last 7 days. @kms-sync-bot include run-ids: run-20260308..run-20260315.
kms-sync-bot: collecting logs, will upload to s3://redwood-security/forensics/1836000000/ (pending)
Olivia Chen: Is there an invariant test we can add to CI that would have caught this? Maybe a property test that ensures org_id(principal) == org_id(target) for all bindings.
Taylor Ng: yes add it to unit tests for the allocator and an integration test for the syncer.
Priya Singh: I filed ticket SEC-4532 to track postmortem, remediation, and customer notification plan. Assigning to Priya (me) and Ajay.
Maria Lopez: quick customer impact check: reach out to support to flag any related incidents and lock affected keys until we confirm.
Kevin Patel: ops-sre confirms kms-sync-runner paused. I'll monitor rollback and re-run a dry-run.
Ajay Rao: Once rollback is complete, let's run a targeted audit query: find any role grants where scope org != principal.org in the last 14 days.
Maria Lopez: running that now. results so far: 5 mismatched grants across 3 small projects (internal), all created by run-20260315.
Olivia Chen: Good catch. No external customers so far. Let's still treat as high severity and follow notification playbook.
Priya Singh: Postmortem owners: Priya (lead), Ajay (root cause), Taylor (tests), Kevin (deploy fixes), Maria (forensics + notifications). I'll post the initial postmortem draft in #postmortems once we have logs.
Taylor Ng: small follow-up: we need to update docs for KMS binding semantics — explicitly call out org_id checks and add an integration test harness.
Ajay Rao: Thanks everyone. Please add any findings to SEC-4532. We’ll reconvene in 2 hours for status update. :thumbsup:
